newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha rises, Malaysian Aug LSWR seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha rises, Malaysian Aug LSWR seen firm.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices gained ground on Tuesday, while Malaysian low-sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) was seen firmer for August in the wake of Indonesian allocations for July as small as 2.3 million barrels, traders said.
Levels for August Malaysian lots were assessed at $1.80 to $1.90 per barrel over the mean of Singapore quotes.
Late last week, 240,000 barrels of Malaysian cargoes were traded at around a $1.70 premium to wrap up July trading, traders said.
Indonesian cargoes for July were bid at about $1.00 per barrel over the Pertamina formula, against no offers.
Fuel oil traders said spot availability for Indonesian July cargoes is expected to remain extremely tight unless Pertamina allocates additional cargoes.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half September was quoted at $199.25/200.50 per tonne. It was sold to a Japanese trading house at $199.00 in late Monday dealing.
Also on Monday, second-half August was traded once at $198.25 and three times at $198.00, traders said.
